acceptance_criteria: No HTTP response carries a value from which the storage path, the vendor or the device identifier can be read.
A named test asserts the response value and fails if a path-shaped value returns.
The server can still resolve an identifier it issued back to its artefact.
The service and frontend suites and the repository privacy gate pass.

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_14H_BACKUP_STEP_SCOPE_PILOT_DEVICE_AND_THE_ASYNCHRONOUS_TRUTH.md (FROZEN) BK-14, with 14I OR-1 carrying the same boundary from the retrieval side.
baseline.observed: The backup-line audit of 2026-09-15 recorded BK-14 and OR-1 as NOT_IMPLEMENTED, with the note that the API omits recovery_volume_path and then returns the same path through another field. Its existing test searches route names only and never inspects a response value, so it passes.

context_not_loaded: The retrieval-audit defect recorded as OR-3 and BK-12, which is a separate movement on different files.
invariants: No new route, and no change to what restore can do.
No artefact byte and no decrypt affordance reaches an HTTP response.
The digest prefix behaviour the class comment describes is unchanged.
report.merge_gate: The worker opens the pull request and does not merge it.
report.objective: The artefact identifier a browser receives stops being the server's storage path. Presentation identity and storage identity become two different values.
output_contract: A SESSION CLOSE on the relay as one NEXUS_SESSION_PACKET.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One value's identity across a store, a controller and two test layers, inside frozen contracts that already state the rule.

requirements: The identifier must be opaque to the receiver and resolvable by the server. State in the pull request how it is derived and why that derivation cannot be reversed into a path by someone holding only the identifier.
AGENTS.md identity law applies: the new identifier is opaque and must not be parsed, split, truncated or compared for structure by any consumer.
The class comment in BackupController is the contract this movement restores. Leave it as the assertion it is, and make the code match it.
risks: A hash of the path is still derived from the path. If the identifier is a digest, say what stops it being used as an oracle against guessed device identifiers.
A test that asserts the identifier is not equal to the path would pass for any wrong value. Assert the property -- that it reveals no segment -- rather than an inequality.

in: Give the browser an opaque identifier that does not reveal the storage layout, the vendor or the device identifier, and that the server can resolve back to the artefact.
Keep the storage path as an internal concern of the store. The manifest may keep whatever it needs; what changes is what leaves the process over HTTP.
A test that inspects the response VALUE, not the route name. The existing test passes today precisely because it only searches route names, and that is the reason this shipped.
A frontend fixture that carries a realistic identifier of the new shape rather than an invented opaque string, so the frontend test would notice a regression.
out: Adding a download, retrieval or decrypt route. BK-13 keeps restore unavailable and no submission surface reaches a restore executor; this movement does not open one.
Changing how or where artefacts are stored, encrypted or digested.
Changing the manifest schema beyond what an opaque presentation identifier requires.
Renaming the artefact_id field. Callers depend on the name; the value changes, not the key.

changed: Added a random UUID presentation_id column and migration; it is generated independently of the storage reference.
Changed backup list summaries to return presentation_id as artefact_id and added a repository resolver from presentation ID to the internal reference.
Added a response-value test that rejects path, vendor, and device segments; updated the frontend fixture to a UUID-shaped identifier.
completed: Prepared the scoped implementation; publication is blocked before commit and pull-request creation.

effects.ui: Frontend fixture only; no runtime UI behavior changed.
